The repo doesn't have app code. The user just wants me to set up a workflow with two jobs where a later job downloads an artifact from an earlier job. I'll create `.github/workflows/artifact-example.yml`.

I should demonstrate the key requirement: `needs` dependency plus `actions/download-artifact`. Also worth noting the artifact action version. As of 2026, `actions/upload-artifact@v4` and `actions/download-artifact@v4` are current. v4 requires unique artifact names and `actions/download-artifact` downloads by name.

Let me create a sensible workflow. I'll keep it generic but functional. Maybe a build job that creates a file, uploads it, then a deploy/test job that downloads it.

input.content:
name: Artifact Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Build output
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          echo "build ${{ github.sha }} at $(date -u +%FT%TZ)" > dist/build-info.txt

      - name: Upload build artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: build-output
          path: dist/
          retention-days: 7

  consume:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Download build artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: build-output
          path: dist

      - name: Use artifact
        run: |
          cat dist/build-info.txt

Done.

Created `.github/workflows/artifact-pipeline.yml`.

The critical pieces:
- `build` job uploads via `actions/upload-artifact` with `name: build-output` (`.github/workflows/artifact-pipeline.yml:19`).
- `consume` job declares `needs: build` so it waits for the upload to finish (line 27), then `actions/download-artifact` pulls the same artifact name (line 31).

Artifact names must match exactly and be unique per upload; with `upload-artifact` v4+ you can't rely on the old behavior of downloading all artifacts without specifying a name.
